items_missed: 1_set_agenda: Never asked 'how are you today,' never checked/confirmed availability for the specific move date, no agenda statement (what she'll cover + rough time), no explicit 'sound good?' confirmation.
2_probe: Didn't ask about stairs/floors at either address, didn't ask about narrow hallways/tight turns, didn't ask about elevator/parking/HOA access, never asked about moving stressors.

3_pricing: No 'pricing is super simple' opener; never explained what's included (gas, truck, taxes, insurance, wrap pads, tools); no mention of disassembly/reassembly despite a bed and chest being on the job; skipped No Worries Damage Coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee, and the full no-hidden-fees pitch.
4_clock: Never explained the clock starts on-site when the contract opens, never mentioned 15-minute prorated increments after the minimum, no explicit sense-check ('does that make sense?').

5_estimate: No typical time range given for a job this size, didn't address stairs/elevator or walk-distance as variables, no assembly/disassembly variable called out despite bed/chest, no equivalents used to help size the job.
6_save_your_ass: Entire section skipped — no prep-before-move-day pitch, no consolidation examples, no carload tip, no sense-check.
7_quote_booking: 'No deposit required' never mentioned, no email/confirmation handoff offered, never asked 'any other questions before I let you go,' never gave hours or how to reach the office.
8_politeness: Used Pete's name only twice (greeting and the book-now attempt) — short of the 3+ target.
9_bonus: No rapport-building or humor beyond patience with a rambling caller, no insurance explanation, no budget-conscious framing despite Pete's clear cost-consciousness.
top_strength: Danah stayed patient and organized through a genuinely hard-to-follow caller — she pulled the zip codes and move-date estimate out of Pete's rambling without getting flustered, and gave clean, accurate tiered pricing: "$192" per two guys on a Thursday versus "$500 for two guys" on Friday/Saturday.
coaching_note: Danah handled a scattered caller well and got the numbers right, but she skipped almost the entire value pitch — no damage coverage, Meet Your Mover, On-Time Guarantee, or no-hidden-fees pitch, and the Save Your Ass prep speech never came up at all. Pete was explicitly weighing cost and worried about rescheduling; that was the moment to sell the peace-of-mind features and float 'no deposit required' as part of the close instead of just describing the reschedule policy. Build a habit of running the full differentiator list every call, even short furniture-only jobs — those are the details that turn 'let me think about it' into a booked move.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and patient with a rambling, hard-to-follow caller, but transactional throughout with no affirmations, empathy statements, or rapport-building beyond the task.
audio_review_reason: Pete dominated the call with long, disjointed statements and ASR-garbled speech, leaving a thin sample of Danah's own language to judge tone from transcript alone.
